task.description: Investigate ISS-0406 (wasm_hang CI flake, ISS-0352's recurrence class, unusually high rate in a multi-session-concurrent window on 2026-09-02) and recommend/implement a safe mitigation if one exists, otherwise resolve as documentation-only against ISS-0352 (the canonical flake-class doc).

result.summary: DIAGNOSIS: read ISS-0406.yaml, ISS-0352.yaml (the full recurrence history: PR #691 original + 4 prior recurrences on PR #780/ISS-0392, PR #786/ISS-0400, PR #790/ISS-0401), .github/workflows/ci.yml, test/test_helper.exs, and lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex. Confirmed: (1) ci.yml runs exactly ONE `ubuntu-latest` job per push/PR (`jobs.backend`), no matrix/partition/parallelism knob of any kind -- this repo's own CI config is not itself amplifying concurrent load; a busy window is caused by multiple sibling sessions' pushes/reruns landing close together on GitHub's shared runner fleet, not by any per-job parallelism setting here. (2) `mix letflow.check.test` (the task CI's `mix letflow.check` alias runs) executes the main suite (`:wasm_hang` excluded, per test_helper.exs) then a SECOND, isolated `mix test --only wasm_hang` subprocess in its own fresh BEAM node -- this isolation (ISS-0352's own prior fix) already prevents the ORIGINAL failure mode (leaked wasmex native threads starving unrelated WASM tests in the SAME process). The residual failure mode this issue is about is entirely WITHIN that isolated subprocess itself. (3) Read the actual 7 `:wasm_hang`-tagged tests (2 in call_timeout_test.exs, 4 in plugin_handler_test.exs, 1 in host_api_write_test.exs) in full. Every one of them dispatches a genuinely, permanently-hanging wasmex NIF call (a real busy-loop .wat fixture) behind a SHORT, FIXED internal timeout bound (100ms-7,000ms: wasmex's own client-side GenServer.call timeout, or PluginInterface's outer Task.yield/2 bound) and asserts the caller's wait is bounded by that short value, not the guest's actual (infinite) runtime. Under normal conditions every one of these tests completes in well under a few seconds; confirmed by this session's own local run (`mix test --only wasm_hang`: `Result: 7 passed, 3058 excluded` in 18.3s). (4) Traced the EXACT mechanism further than any prior ISS-0352 recurrence note: `plugin_handler_test.exs`'s AC4 test ("a 300ms timeout_ms binds sooner than a 7_000ms timeout_ms...") failed on the ISS-0352/PR #786 recurrence not via ExUnit's 60,000ms per-test timeout (the failure mode every OTHER recurrence note describes) but via its OWN explicit `assert long_elapsed_ms < 15_000` assertion, observed at `long_elapsed_ms: 30_003`ms for a call configured with only a 7,000ms wasmex-level timeout -- i.e. BEAM's own scheduling/timer delivery for that call took over 4x its configured bound. This is diagnostic: it rules OUT Postgres connection-pool exhaustion as the mechanism (each CI job in ci.yml gets its OWN dedicated `services.postgres` container -- there is no DB shared ACROSS concurrent CI runs/jobs to exhaust; and the isolated `:only wasm_hang` subprocess runs alone, after the main suite finishes, with zero other concurrent DB-heavy work inside that same subprocess to contend for connections). What it IS consistent with: CPU-scheduling delay -- host-level CPU contention on GitHub Actions' shared runner fleet (multiple concurrent jobs from this repo's own sibling sessions, or noisy-neighbor VMs on the same physical host, both outside this repo's control) starves the BEAM scheduler of the CPU time it needs to service its own timer wheel and deliver the GenServer.call-timeout/Task.yield messages promptly, so a call that SHOULD return around its configured bound instead measures much longer wall-clock elapsed time, or in worse cases exceeds ExUnit's own 60,000ms per-test ceiling entirely. This session's own corroborating observation (PRs #788, #792, #798, #801 -- 4 completely unrelated diffs -- each hit multiple wasm_hang rounds, always clearing on rerun with zero code changes, one duplicate run on PR #798 took over an hour) reinforces the resource-contention hypothesis at a volume beyond any prior single-recurrence data point. CONCLUSION ON THE 4 REQUESTED QUESTIONS: (1) mechanism is CPU/scheduling delay on a contended CI runner, not Postgres pool exhaustion, not a per-test flakiness bug in the WASM/wasmex code itself. (2) no CI-side parallelism knob in this repo amplifies it; the isolated-subprocess structure ISS-0352 already put in place is correct and unchanged-worthy. (3) a concrete, safe, bounded-downside mitigation DOES exist and was implemented (see below) -- raising the wasm_hang tests' own ExUnit timeout, plus loosening the one test whose failure mode is an explicit numeric assertion rather than the ExUnit timeout itself. (4) the DEEPER fix (eliminating the mechanism, not just tolerating more jitter) is GitHub Actions infrastructure-level (larger/dedicated runners) and/or the already-filed OQ-5 structural fix (an operator-configurable cap on concurrently in-flight WASM invocations, req170 design doc §8) -- both out of scope for this session; documented as the load-bearing follow-up. MITIGATION IMPLEMENTED (verified locally, not merely proposed): added `@tag timeout: 180_000` (raised from ExUnit's 60,000ms default) to all 7 `:wasm_hang`-tagged tests across test/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout_test.exs, plugin_handler_test.exs, and host_api_write_test.exs; loosened plugin_handler_test.exs's AC4 test's own explicit `long_elapsed_ms < 15_000` assertion to `< 45_000` (the ONE failure mode a raised @tag timeout alone cannot fix, since it's a numeric assertion, not an ExUnit-level timeout) while leaving its `long_elapsed_ms > 6_000` discriminator (rules out timeout_ms being silently dropped to wasmex's hardcoded 5,000ms default) untouched. SAFETY ARGUMENT (verified, not assumed): every one of these tests still waits on the SAME internal, short, fixed timeout mechanism under test -- the raised ceiling only absorbs scheduling jitter around an already-short expected duration. If the timeout mechanism itself ever broke and stopped firing for real (a genuine regression, not jitter), the test would still eventually hit the new, later ceiling and fail -- no hang-detection capability is removed, only the tolerance for how much CI-runner jitter is treated as a false failure. VERIFICATION PERFORMED LOCALLY (real command output, not speculation): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- clean, zero output. `mix format --check-formatted` -- clean, zero output. `mix test --only wasm_hang` -- `Result: 7 passed, 3058 excluded` in 18.3s (all 7 wasm_hang tests, including the newly-tagged/loosened ones, pass under normal, uncontended local conditions). Full `mix letflow.check.test` (CI's own exact invocation, main suite + isolated wasm_hang subprocess): main suite result `3053/3055 passed (6/6 properties, 3047/3049 tests), 10 excluded`, 2 failures -- both in `test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_toolchain_test.exs` ("a matching rust pin reports OK...", "a mismatched rust pin reports a MISMATCH row..."), both `** (ErlangError) Erlang error: :enoent` from `System.cmd("rustc", ["--version"], ...)` -- confirmed as a LOCAL-SANDBOX-ONLY environment artifact (rustc not resolvable via this shell's PATH inside the test subprocess's environment), entirely unrelated to this session's diff (that test file is untouched by this fix, tests toolchain-pin detection logic, not WASM/wasmex) and unrelated to ISS-0406/ISS-0352's own mechanism; CI's own `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` step installs rustc on the PATH before `mix letflow.check` runs, so this is not expected to reproduce in CI. `letflow.check.test`'s wasm_hang second subprocess never ran in that particular invocation because the task's `run/1` raises on the first (main-suite) subprocess's nonzero exit before reaching `run_wasm_hang_tests/0` -- already independently verified clean via the standalone `mix test --only wasm_hang` run above (7 passed). ISS-0406 marked `status: resolved` with the mitigation detail. ISS-0352 (canonical flake-class doc) appended with a fifth recurrence note carrying this session's full corroborating data (PRs #788/#792/#798/#801), the refined mechanism diagnosis, and the mitigation detail -- left as the durable home for this recurrence class per its own established pattern.
result.recommendation_to_orch: No further routing to CODE-DESIGNER needed -- this is a small, safe, already-implemented and already-verified test-only change (7 `@tag timeout: 180_000` additions plus one numeric assertion-bound loosening, no production code touched, no new design surface). Recommend ORCH treat this as a direct action: review the diff (test/letflow/engine/wasm/call_timeout_test.exs, plugin_handler_test.exs, host_api_write_test.exs, docs/issues/ISS-0406.yaml, docs/issues/ISS-0352.yaml), then commit/push/open PR/merge per the standard humanless flow -- no CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR or SECURITY-REVIEWER gate is needed for a test-timeout/assertion-tolerance change with no tenant-data-path or OTP-supervision-shape implications. Flag for future prioritization (not this session's scope): the OQ-5 structural fix (operator-configurable cap on concurrently in-flight WASM invocations, req170 design doc §8) is the only fix that ELIMINATES this mechanism rather than tolerating more CI-runner jitter -- now supported by five independent recurrences (PR #691, PR #780/ISS-0392, PR #786/ISS-0400, PR #790/ISS-0401, this session's multi-PR window/ISS-0406) and should be considered for its own requirement rather than continuing to be deferred. Also worth flagging to whoever owns CI infra decisions: if this mitigation's 180s ceiling still proves insufficient (the PR #798 "over an hour" duplicate-run outlier suggests contention magnitudes exist that no reasonable per-test timeout bump can absorb), the next lever is GitHub Actions runner sizing/dedication, which is outside this repo's own config entirely.
